title: Safety Before Style: A Risk-and-Accuracy Audit of Tools, Knife Skills, Equipment, and Hygiene in a Foundational Cookery Manuscript
abstract: This study evaluated the safety, technical accuracy, and risk communication of a 59-page illustrated foundational cookery manuscript. A structured document audit examined cooking terms, knives and tools, cookware, appliances, cutting techniques, napkin-folding instructions, and the final hygiene unit. The manuscript introduces several useful safety concepts, but safety is often separated from practice rather than embedded at the point of hazard. The article proposes a hazard-at-point-of-use model, critical stop rules, measurable controls, and a staged technical, safety, accessibility, and classroom validation protocol.

title: Beyond Picture Naming: An Evidence-Centered Assessment Redesign for a Foundational Cookery Manuscript
abstract: This study examined the assessment architecture of a 59-page illustrated foundational cookery manuscript. Structured document analysis mapped seven content units, their printed explanations, 153 scorable prompts, and the forms of learner evidence they solicit. Most assessment evidence is limited to recognition and recall, with insufficient demonstration, performance criteria, feedback, or reassessment. The article proposes a seven-unit evidence map and a four-part performance portfolio covering planning, monitored execution, product evidence, and reflective justification.

title: Learning Entrepreneurship by Doing: A Case-Based and Performance-Assessment Design for Teacher Education
abstract: Entrepreneurship education can become overly declarative when learners memorize traits, ownership forms, planning steps, and advertising types without making decisions under uncertainty. This conceptual article develops a case-based, performance-assessment design organized around noticing opportunities, mobilizing resources, testing value, and communicating a defensible venture decision. It proposes a progressive venture portfolio, authentic evidence, and analytic rubrics while separating entrepreneurial learning from business success.

title: Screening Local Venture Ideas: A Five-Gate Model for Community Entrepreneurship
abstract: Community entrepreneurship is frequently taught as the search for a promising idea, yet a viable opportunity requires evidence of a customer problem, an implementable solution, a sustainable operating model, and acceptable social consequences. This conceptual article develops a structured opportunity-screening framework integrating community-needs inquiry, capability review, external analysis, resource fit, value-proposition testing, and small-scale validation. A five-gate screening matrix and field-interview protocol are proposed.

title: Adapting Marungko Sound Blending to English: A Cumulative Path from Decoding to Sentence Comprehension
abstract: Marungko-inspired materials introduce sounds in a purposeful sequence and move learners from letters to syllables, words, phrases, and sentences. This conceptual-design article proposes an orthographic-alignment framework for adapting that logic to English phonology, word meaning, grammar, and connected-text comprehension. It offers an audit matrix and a six-phase lesson cycle moving through oral sound analysis, grapheme mapping, blending, sentence reading, meaning construction, and encoding.

title: Validating Student Microventures: An Evidence-Based Model for Product Positioning and Market Communication
abstract: Student entrepreneurship projects often culminate in attractive promotions before learners establish whether a product solves a meaningful problem. This conceptual practice article develops an evidence-driven market-to-message framework connecting customer problem, value proposition, minimum product evidence, selling conversation, and channel-appropriate message. It proposes a traceable claim system, classroom implementation sequence, and rubric focused on evidence, coherence, ethics, and iteration.

title: Cultivating Enterprising Educators: A Community-Value Competency Framework for Teacher Preparation
abstract: Entrepreneurship education is frequently reduced to business-plan writing or lists of desirable traits. This conceptual practice article offers a competency-based sequence moving students from self-awareness to opportunity recognition, disciplined experimentation, market engagement, and reflection on community value. It proposes a five-stage learning architecture, an aligned assessment strategy, and safeguards against trait essentialism and unsupported economic-impact claims.

title: Embedding Research Integrity From Proposal to Publication
abstract: Research ethics is frequently confined to informed consent forms or a final lecture on plagiarism. This conceptual article argues that integrity must be embedded across the complete research lifecycle. It presents a six-stage model covering problem selection, design, participant engagement, data stewardship, analysis and reporting, and publication, translating ethical duties into practical questions and classroom supports.

title: Literature Reviewing as an Architecture of Researchable Problems
abstract: A literature review is often taught as a preliminary collection of sources, yet its more important function is to construct a defensible research problem. This conceptual article reframes reviewing as an architecture of claims, relationships, and unresolved questions. It distinguishes six review purposes and proposes a workflow for delimiting the problem space, retrieving and evaluating evidence, coding claims, synthesizing relationships, and converting tensions into research questions.

title: Teaching Research Frameworks Through Purposeful Design Alignment
abstract: Research methods courses often present qualitative and quantitative inquiry as competing traditions or lists of procedures to memorize. This conceptual article proposes design alignment as a more productive organizing principle. It connects five decisions—the problem, research questions, evidence, analytic procedures, and warranted claims—and offers a classroom sequence, practical alignment audit, and assessments for proposal development and formative feedback.
